request:
# refactor(cli): public application API and container-free CLI

One slice of the application-boundaries refactor. **Treat this request as self-contained**: everything needed is below and in `docs/specs/application-boundaries.md`. Do not assume access to the parent issue or its siblings.

Lands after the issue that moves the GitHub code out of `src/integrations`, and builds on it. The
construction-mechanism issue lands after this one.

## What

Every jig operation can be invoked without the command line, with the same preparation, safety
checks and cleanup. The command line only reads input, calls the operation and shows the result.

## Why

Command handlers currently check the repository, load configuration, create the application and
dispose of it themselves. Any other caller would have to repeat all of that and could get it wrong.
Moving that responsibility behind an application boundary keeps it in one place.

## Context — read this first

jig is a TypeScript CLI that turns a markdown request into planned slices, has agents implement and
review each one in a sandbox, and lands them on one run branch. Source owners under `src/`:
`domain` (business rules), `ports` (external capability contracts), `config` (settings schemas and
policy), `flow`/`steps` (workflow execution), `prompts`, `observers` (events and reporting),
`adapters` (Git, GitHub, files, containers, terminal, logging), `app` (use cases) and `cli` (commands).
Specs sit beside the code they cover (`foo.ts` → `foo.spec.ts`). Before editing, read `AGENTS.md`,
the house rules in `.claude/rules/` that cover the files you change, and `docs/architecture.html`.

This issue implements one part of the design in `docs/specs/application-boundaries.md`. That file is
in the repository; read the sections named below. Where this issue and the spec disagree, follow
the spec and say so in the PR.

## Don't undo these

- Agents run unattended only inside the sandbox. Never add an agent call that runs on the host.
- Credentials never land in a file jig writes, a log line or the image. The one exception:
  `jig init` saves a credential to `.jig/.env` (owner-only, git-ignored) after the operator agrees.
- Nothing touches the target repository's tracked files outside the run's worktree.
- Keep commands, flags, defaults, help, error tags and messages, exit codes, configuration
  precedence and recovery behavior unchanged unless this issue says otherwise.
- Expected failures are `Result` values; bugs panic. jig never throws.
- Keep dependency policy in `.dependency-cruiser.mjs` and `scripts/check-dependencies.mjs`, with
  fixtures in `scripts/check-dependencies.spec.ts`. Do not write another source scanner.
- No release tags and no version bumps; `main` publishes on its own.
- If you change where something lives, update `docs/architecture.html`, `docs/workflow-ownership.md`
  and the code map in `CONTRIBUTING.md`, and any guide that names a moved path. Describe current
  behavior in the present tense.

## Target

Spec sections: "CLI and the incoming application API", "Application preparation and resource
lifetime", "Acceptance evidence" items 2–4, 6 and 7.

Current leaks:

- `src/cli/with-app.ts` (`withApp`, `processInvocation`) runs repository checks, loads credentials,
  resolves configuration and presets, creates the container and disposes of it.
- `src/cli/app-action.ts` and `src/cli/commands/*.ts`, and the GitHub command, receive
  `AwilixContainer<AppCradle>` or cradle access.
- `src/app/run-jig.ts`, `run-status.ts`, `run-stores.ts`, `init-sandbox.ts` and
  `throwaway-sandbox.ts` take the container or cradle.

Required:

- Declare a public app entry (`src/app/api.ts` or `src/app/api/`). It covers: start/resume a run,
  status, init, build the sandbox image, list presets, and implement a GitHub issue. It may export
  the real use-case functions; do not add a parallel facade/service/contract layer unless it hides
  real preparation or lifecycle. Inputs and outputs expose no Awilix type, cradle, concrete store,
  Pino logger, OpenTelemetry tracer, Commander command, `process`/environment object or terminal
  adapter. Do not infer exported types from concrete factories when that leaks their types.
- Split `with-app` by responsibility, following the spec's preparation table. Composition captures
  arguments, working directory and environment sources and picks the terminal/logging
  implementations. CLI parses syntax and translates file/stdin input through supplied capabilities.
  Config validates and resolves. Adapters do file, Git and credential I/O. App decides repository
  prerequisites, credential-source policy, required stores and preparation order. Operations do not
  read process globals.
- Keep the current per-operation preparation order, especially refusing bad input before opening
  resources. Help and version start nothing. Status and ended-run queries keep their existing
  environment and saved-credential loading and failures, never prompt for agent credentials, and
  never start a sandbox.
- Lifecycle wrappers acquire, invoke and release together. If work fails, the work failure wins and
  a cleanup failure is reported. If work succeeds, a cleanup failure replaces the success. Attempt
  every release in order. With several cleanup failures and no work failure, return the first and
  report the rest. Release what was already acquired when a later acquisition fails. After a work
  panic, run cleanup and keep the original cause for reporting; a panic stays a bug. Close the
  sandbox before scope disposal, and keep the telemetry/output flush order.
- Init's agent selection, credential-save consent and preset cancellation go through narrow
  operator-interaction ports. App decides when a choice is needed; the terminal adapter renders it.
  Do not invent a non-interactive protocol.
- The container may remain inside app for now (a separate spike decides its future). No CLI file
  may name it.
- Lint: CLI may import app only through the public entry; other app paths are private to app and
  composition. Add fixtures for an allowed entry import, a rejected deep import, and a type-only leak.

## Done when

- [ ] `grep -rnE "Awilix|Cradle|withApp" src/cli` finds nothing.
- [ ] Each operation has a behavior test through the public entry with fakes, without importing
      CLI, constructing Awilix or reaching an adapter implementation.
- [ ] Tests cover: preparation failure before sandbox start, preset cancellation, invalid
      file/stdin input, init cancellation and save consent, run-lock refusal, work failure plus
      cleanup failure, success plus cleanup failure, partial acquisition failure, and work panic
      with original-cause reporting.
- [ ] Status stays non-mutating and starts no sandbox. Custom run stores, start/resume identity and
      publication recovery still work.
- [ ] The verification below passes.

## Verification

From the repository root using the pinned Node version (`volta` in `package.json`):

```sh
npm run lint:dependencies
npm run lint
npm run typecheck
npm test
npm run build
npm run format:check
npm run validate -- --skip test:mutation
```

No check may start an agent on the host or publish to GitHub. In the PR, state which owner each
moved concept now belongs to and why.


Source: https://github.com/ygrishajev/jig/issues/58

context.repoSummary:
The repository is a TypeScript ESM CLI using Commander, Zod, better-result, Awilix and Vitest. GitHub redistribution is already present: src/composition/main.ts owns executable startup, src/cli/commands/github.ts declares commands, src/app/implement-issue.ts coordinates execution/publication, and ports/adapters provide external capabilities. There is no public app entry yet.

src/cli/with-app.ts currently checks the repository, parses environment, loads saved credentials, resolves config/presets, constructs the container and disposes it. app-action.ts parses and prepares command input before opening resources; run file/stdin translation and GitHub settings preparation preserve important early-failure ordering. Commands import private app modules and access the cradle. run-jig.ts owns locking, start/resume identity, ended-run detection, execution and artefacts; run-status.ts uses store.peek and local metrics. run-stores.ts selects and constructs built-in/custom stores. init-sandbox.ts handles agent selection, credential consent and sandbox verification. container.ts, throwaway-sandbox.ts and report-cleanup.ts contain existing lifecycle and cleanup precedence behavior, with concrete logging/session types leaking across boundaries.

docs/specs/application-boundaries.md defines the requested portable operation API and responsibility split: composition captures sources and wires implementations; CLI translates input/presents results; config resolves policy; adapters perform I/O; app owns prerequisites, preparation and resource lifetime. Preserve saved-credential failures for status, sandbox-free ended-run queries, custom stores, publication recovery and original panic causes. Existing colocated specs cover many behaviors but need public-entry coverage through fakes without containers/adapters. Dependency enforcement belongs in .dependency-cruiser.mjs and scripts/check-dependencies.mjs, with fixtures in scripts/check-dependencies.spec.ts; CLI public-entry restrictions are still needed. Ownership changes also require updates to docs/architecture.html, docs/workflow-ownership.md and CONTRIBUTING.md. The pinned Node version is 26.13.0; requested validation includes dependency lint, lint, typecheck, tests, build, formatting and validate with mutation testing skipped.

plan.summary: Introduce src/app/api.ts as the portable entry for start/resume, status, init, sandbox-image build, preset listing and GitHub issue implementation. Move operation preparation and lifecycle policy out of CLI handlers, replace container/cradle parameters with narrow capabilities, and preserve existing behavior, safety guarantees and recovery.
plan.approach: First characterize each operation's current preparation and release sequence, including early file/stdin and GitHub-settings failures. Reuse the existing GitHub redistribution and config I/O separation rather than rebuilding them. Composition captures arguments, working directory and environment sources, selects implementations and binds operations lazily. CLI retains syntax parsing, file/stdin translation through supplied capabilities, presentation and exit codes; app owns repository prerequisites, credential-source decisions, required stores, preparation order and lifecycle; config retains validation and resolution; adapters perform I/O. Export actual use cases or wrappers that own meaningful preparation, with explicit portable contracts and no application-wide dependency bag. Move init choices and consent behind narrow operator-interaction ports, keeping cancellation explicit. Keep GitHub execution on the same run implementation, preserving locks, identity, custom stores and publication recovery. Lifecycle wrappers acquire, invoke and release together: release partially acquired resources, attempt every release in order, close sandboxes before scopes, preserve telemetry/output flush order, retain work failures over reported cleanup failures, return the first cleanup failure after successful work, and preserve original panic causes. Status remains non-mutating; status and ended-run queries retain saved-credential loading and failures without credential prompts or sandbox startup. Help/version remain resource-free. Design must resolve an explicit sequencing mismatch: the request permits containers inside app and places construction work afterward, while the spec prohibits container dependencies in use cases, selects composition for concrete wiring, and gates container-specific planning on spike #49. Follow the spec, record the conflict in the eventual PR, and leave the mechanism decision gated rather than silently retaining container-dependent use cases or prescribing a container rewrite. Current house rules also describe app-only construction, so reconcile those with the selected boundary. Another acceptance distinction is that invalid file/stdin handling belongs in CLI boundary tests, while every operation needs independent public-entry tests; do not move transport parsing into app merely to combine these tests. Add fake-capability API tests for every operation and the required preparation, cancellation, consent, lock, cleanup, partial-acquisition and panic cases, plus observer exception isolation and panic propagation. Preserve real temporary-repository adapter tests. Enforce CLI imports exclusively through the public entry and private-app access only from app/composition using the existing dependency tooling, including allowed-entry, rejected-deep-import and type-only-leak fixtures; review transitive exported types with meaningful compile-time coverage. Update ownership documentation and affected path references. Validate with pinned Node 26.13.0 using dependency lint, lint, typecheck, tests, build, formatting and validate with mutation testing skipped, without host agent execution or GitHub publication.
affectedAreas: src/app/api.ts and colocated public-entry behavior/type coverage: operation contracts, preparation and portable outcomes.
src/app/run-jig.ts, run-status.ts, run-stores.ts and implement-issue.ts: narrow dependencies, store selection, shared run execution and preserved recovery.
src/app/init-sandbox.ts, throwaway-sandbox.ts, report-cleanup.ts and container.ts: interaction policy, acquisition/release boundaries and construction-policy reconciliation.
src/cli/with-app.ts, app-action.ts, main.ts, commands/*.ts and input/option helpers: remove preparation, concrete dependencies and all Awilix, Cradle and withApp references.
src/composition/main.ts and composition wiring: capture sources, bind portable operations, select adapters and observers, preserve lazy startup and shutdown.
src/ports and relevant filesystem, Git, local-store, sandbox, terminal, logging and telemetry adapters: portable capabilities and concrete I/O/resource implementations.
src/config environment, configuration, preset and GitHub-settings contracts: preserve existing pure resolution and precedence while relocating orchestration.
src/app/observed-events.ts, observability/report contracts and observer wiring: portable metrics, failure isolation and original-cause reporting.
.dependency-cruiser.mjs, scripts/check-dependencies.mjs and scripts/check-dependencies.spec.ts: enforce the public-entry boundary including type-only dependencies.
Colocated CLI, app, composition and adapter specs plus tests/support: behavioral regression coverage and reusable capability fakes.
docs/architecture.html, docs/workflow-ownership.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, affected public path references and applicable .claude/rules: accurate ownership and resolved construction guidance.
